// THE STATE OF THE SCENE

Modification isn't a niche anymore

What used to live in garage forums and late-night meet-ups now drives mainstream car culture. Widebody kits, forced-induction builds, and livery wraps that once marked out a small drift-and-tuner crowd are now standard vocabulary for anyone under thirty scrolling a For You page.

Social platforms turned individual builds into full media careers — a single well-shot reveal can outperform a manufacturer's own launch campaign. That shift has pulled money, sponsorships, and serious engineering talent into a space that used to run on pure enthusiasm alone.

The result is a modification scene that's faster, more visually ambitious, and more technically capable than it's ever been — and it's no longer hiding at the edges of the automotive world.
